title: HEAD_DIM 64 + Muon LR 0.04 -> 0.055
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (10 heads of 64 at unchanged n_embd 640) plus MATRIX_LR 0.04->0.055; DEPTH 10, ASPECT_RATIO 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 and all other LRs unchanged.
reflection: val_bpb 1.000971 vs the 0.988076 baseline: +0.0129, ~27 sigma on the pooled 4.8e-4 floor. A strong NEGATIVE for raising the Muon LR. 1085 steps, 284.4M tokens, MFU 40.67%, peak VRAM 33.8GB, final smoothed train loss 2.806 vs the baseline's 2.752. My run contains HEAD_DIM 64, which a2 measured at -0.0038 and which the pure-HD64 arm this round measures directly, so the +37% Muon LR alone cost roughly +0.017. I proposed the up direction in advance and argued for it from the flat batch curve (2^19->2^17 moved val_bpb by 8e-5, which I read as gradient noise not being the binding constraint, i.e. a step size on the small side). That inference was wrong: MATRIX_LR 0.04 is at or above the optimum, so the only useful remaining LR probe is downward (0.03), and the flat batch curve says nothing about where the LR sits. One clean side fact, the first throughput cost anyone has measured for HEAD_DIM 64: MFU 40.67% vs the baseline's 41.94% and 1085 steps vs 1119, i.e. ten heads of 64 are about 3% slower in FA3 than five of 128 at the same dim. That is small and the pure-HD64 arm should still win, but HEAD_DIM 64 is not literally free in wall-clock, only in params, FLOPs and VRAM.
